messages:
maria_ops: Heads-up — after the role-boundary hardening change this morning, the cluster-autoscaler in eu-central started failing to assume the provisioning role. Seeing GPU warm pools drop and pending pods stacking. :rotating_light:

samir_infra: omg, do you have the error logs?

maria_ops: pasted the most relevant bit from the node-provisioner logs:
```
2026-03-20T09:17:03Z ERROR assume-role failed: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/cluster-autoscaler/instance is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/provisioner-eu
status code: 403
```

jen_security: we rolled the role-boundary policy to prevent cross-account chaining — it's supposed to block wide hyphened principals. Did the provisioner role have an explicit `sts:AssumeRole` trust for the autoscaler principal?

maria_ops: it did before the change. The change tightened `iam:PassedToService` / role boundary conditions. I suspect the autoscaler's instance profile no longer matches the new boundary.

lee_oncall: quick question — is this only affecting GPU node groups or all node groups? Customer impact scope? :eyes: 

samir_infra: only GPU node groups so far. Non-GPU pools are fine. Likely because GPU pools use a different provisioner role (provisioner-eu-gpu) with broader assumed principals.

maria_ops: Current symptom: GPU warm pool size goes to 0, pods Pending with `0/10 nodes are available`. Autoscaler logs show repeated `AccessDenied` from sts. We throttled scale-down but can't scale up.

jen_security: if it helps — I can temporarily add a scoped exception for `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/cluster-autoscaler/*` to the boundary to verify. But prefer we do a minimal allow for the GPU provisioner only.

samir_infra: that would be great. Also, can someone confirm whether the role boundary change also touched KMS grants used by the GPU boot scripts? We had a KMS decrypt step during node bootstrap.

maria_ops: KMS decrypts are failing sporadically too, but I think that's separate — probably due to tight key policy we rolled last week. Error snippet:
```
Error: kms:Decrypt not authorized for key arn:aws:kms:eu-central-1:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh-... while decrypting bootstrap token
```

jen_security: ok — two separate vectors (IAM/sts + KMS). I'll scope the role-boundary exception first so autoscaler can recover. Then we can coordinate a tighter KMS grant with ops.

lee_oncall: can we put a temporary routing rule to use on-demand non-GPU nodes for critical traffic until GPU capacity returns? We have a couple of prod tenants seeing degraded throughput.

samir_infra: I can gate traffic by label `gpu-required=true` and evict/migrate noncritical workloads. Will take ~15m.

deploy-bot: @channel automated alert: 3 pods in namespace `vision-core` pending > 10m due to nodegroup capacity in eu-central-1. Incident link: https://redwood.inc/incident/INC-2026-143

maria_ops: thanks. jen, whenever you add the exception ping here and I'll validate autoscaler can assume. After that we'll run a rolling bootstrap for GPU warm pools.

jen_security: exception applied for `provisioner-eu-gpu` principal at 09:24 UTC, boundary scope limited to `sts:AssumeRole` only.

samir_infra: confirming, autoscaler now shows successful AssumeRole at 09:24:12. GPU warm pool rebuild started. :thumbsup:

maria_ops: warm pool +3 nodes coming up, pods draining from pending queue. I'll keep monitoring KMS decrypt errors separately and open a follow-up issue for key grant tightening.

jen_security: opened SEC-2026-71 to track KMS policy reconciliation and least-privilege rollout. Assigning to @jen_security + @samir_infra.

lee_oncall: nice quick response team — recommend we document this in runbook: link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/iam-role-boundary-gpu.md and add a pre-change checklist for role-boundary rollouts.

maria_ops: agreed, adding checklist items now. Closing thread when everything stable. :white_check_mark:
